host: EC2 c7i.4xlarge in us-east-2, Xeon Platinum 8488C, Linux. One pinned CPU per process. Other experiments occupied separate physical cores.

lower_bound.scope: Constructively reachable subset, including individual honest knowledge sets; full graph cardinality and universal Inv are separate questions.

face_module: FaceMsgs == { [type |-> "1b", acc |-> a, bal |-> b, mbal |-> -1,
mval |-> None, m2av |-> {}] : a \in FakeAcceptor, b \in 0..(K-1) }
face_cfg: Append CONSTANT K = 1, 2, or 3 and CONSTRAINT Face or CONSTRAINT Unheard to original CFG. Retain SPECIFICATION Spec and INVARIANT Inv.

commands.core: dive check Face.tla --config CFG --library-path LIB --store exact --workers 1 --seed 0 --fp 0 --max-memory 1500m --time-limit 180s --output json
commands.replay: dive validate-trace BPConProof.tla --config BPConProof.cfg --library-path LIB --trace TRACE --seed 0 --fp 0 --output json

dimension_assertions.test: Face-1 under the original constants and Inv. Both Core exact and pinned TLC passed all three assumptions and reached 9 states, depth 5.

replay.recipe: Begin in the original Init. For each of the three ballots send three fake 1b records, two 2av and two 2b records and both 1c values, then one 1a. For 1b index j=0,1,2 choose mbal=j-1, mval=(None,v1,v2)[j] and m2av containing pairs for ballots 0..j-1 with alternating values. For the nine 1b messages numbered 0..8, deliver each to the subset of the three honest nodes selected by the low three bits of its number. Each delivery takes one original acceptor step. Give each finite trace a behavior ending. Append one step deleting a sent record as the negative control.

invariance.run: tlapm --threads 1 --nofp -k BPConProof.tla, single pinned logical CPU on c7i.4xlarge. Each source set has its own cache. No previous obligation fingerprints used.
invariance.sources: Copy BPConProof, PConProof, VoteProof and Consensus from the pinned Examples source. Cut the root immediately after the closing BY <1>1, <1>2, PTL DEF Spec of THEOREM Invariance, and finish the module with ==== . Keep the original proof text. Copy crates/dive-sema/bundled/tlaps/FiniteSetTheorems.tla beside the sources. The finite arm replaces Ballot == Nat in BPConProof, PConProof and VoteProof with Ballot == {b \in Nat : b <= 2}. The supplementary imported PConProof NextDef prefix ends after BY <1>2, <1>3 DEF Next, TLANext; run tlapm on that prefix separately.
invariance.trust: The pinned finite set induction theorem and other standard mathematical library lemmas are premises supplied by the indicated libraries. The measured property is Spec => []Inv. Refinement theorems after Invariance are outside this experiment.
invariance.earlier_trials: With the installer library and literal 0..2 only in the root, the finite trial missed 4/744. The original Nat trial missed 1/744. The published library corrects the finite-set-induction statement used in this source and the finite proof specializes imported definitions consistently.
invariance.cfg_controls: Core and TLC with the released constants passed the original startup assumptions and the explicit assumptions None \notin Value and Ballot = {0,1,2}. Changing the invariant to Inv /\ bmsgs={} fails at depth two with a replayable violation (Core 0.12 s / 72,648 KiB; TLC 2.06 s / 252,656 KiB). No complete graph counts follow from these proofs.

configured_invariance.scope: BPConProof.cfg selects SPECIFICATION Spec and INVARIANT Inv. The specialized theorem proves Spec => []Inv for each fresh value outside Value and for the root assumptions. TLC checks the released root assignments and assumptions. The released CFG overrides root operators only. Spec and Inv use neither imported P!Ballot nor P!None, so specializing these imported definitions in the proof preserves the configured root property. Later refinement, agreement and liveness claims are outside the theorem, as is total graph cardinality.
configured_invariance.preparation: scripts/perf/scale/bpcon_proof.py reads the pinned CFG, four Examples modules and the bundled finite-set library. It truncates the root after Invariance, specializes the three Ballot definitions and replaces the two mathematical-choice sentinels with one shared FreshNone parameter. Two changes to proofs establish the imported freshness premise and split the Phase2b acceptor ballot-bound step. Init, Next, Spec and Inv retain their source definitions.
configured_invariance.assumptions: None is distinct from the two proposals. Ballot and -1 are disjoint from the four model-value acceptors. The three good acceptors are disjoint from the fake one. All Byzantine quorums are subsets of their union and every ordered pair of Byzantine quorums shares a good acceptor. Each weak quorum is a subset containing a good acceptor. Each family has an all-good member. Projecting each Byzantine quorum onto the good set gives the four intersecting quorums of P!QA.
configured_invariance.dependencies: PNextDef cites P!NextDef, explicitly discharging P!QA, P!BallotAssump and P!NoneOutside. PNextDef is first used after Invariance, in the later refinement proof. The isolated PConProof prefix ends at NextDef before the VoteProof instance. The proof imports mathematical library statements, including FS_Induction. TLAPS loading VoteProof and Consensus did not certify those modules' theorems.
configured_invariance.host: EC2 c7i.4xlarge, Xeon Platinum 8488C, Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64. Other jobs could run on the host. Times and peak RSS come from GNU time. Fingerprint reuse and worker counts differ between the two root runs.

commands.root_cached: timeout -k 10 3200 taskset -c 6 tlapm --threads 1 -k BPConProof.tla (7 GiB cgroup, previously populated fingerprints loaded)
commands.root_cold: timeout -k 10 3200 taskset -c 5,6 tlapm --threads 2 --nofp -k BPConProof.tla (8 GiB cgroup, fresh work directory)
commands.nextdef_cold: timeout 300 taskset -c 4 tlapm --threads 1 --nofp -k PConProof.tla (4 GiB cgroup, independent prefix)

configured_invariance.intermediate_trials: The initial named-sentinel run retained the two original proof steps. The next trial introduced the imported freshness premise and tried SMT on the unsplit Phase2b goal. The final source splits that goal into the message membership and ballot bound, with the latter proved from the function update.

proof_mapping.claims: For the transformed proof modules, Ballot equals 0..2 and P!Ballot. P!None, None and FreshNone are equal, and None is outside Value. These equalities describe the specialized proof instance.

config_control.source: Original Examples modules. The helper retains all constant assignments and Inv, adds a second binding for the named None atom, and selects Init with a single stuttering step. ConfigCheck uses the original BQA, BQLA, BallotAssump, and projected P!QA. It checks the ballot domain, projected ballot disjointness, and named None outside Value.

original_instance_controls.recipe: In a copy of config/ConfigCheck.tla rename the module to OriginalInstance and insert one ASSUME Extra before Stay. Run pinned TLC with ConfigCheck.cfg. Each probe changes only the indicated assumption.

imported_sentinel_equal.result: TLC cannot evaluate the unbounded CHOOSE at PConProof.tla:111

original_instance_controls.unused_instance: In the specialized root prefix remove the P == INSTANCE PConProof declaration and only the PNextDef lemma and its proof. Pinned tla2sany.SANY resolves BPConProof with FiniteSetTheorems and the TLAPS library, with PConProof, VoteProof and Consensus absent. This checks that the remaining root definitions and Invariance proof have no references to the instance.

configured_invariance.input_integrity_control: Appended a comment to each of the six pinned inputs separately. Each preparation exited 1, named the altered file and created no output directory. The generated proof modules and the isolated NextDef prefix reproduced the measured byte hashes.

ordinary_core_capacity.host: Matched isolated EC2 r7i.16xlarge, Xeon Platinum 8488C, 32 physical cores, GNU time. Default fingerprint identity, original BPConProof.tla and CFG.
ordinary_core_capacity.args: taskset -c 0-31 ./row-spans check specifications/byzpaxos/BPConProof.tla --config specifications/byzpaxos/BPConProof.cfg --library-path modules --workers 32 --compat=tlc --fp 0 --seed 0 --max-memory CAPg --time-limit SECONDSs --output json
ordinary_core_capacity.interpretation: Both runs stopped on memory at depth four. More than 99.8% of admitted fingerprints were queued in both. The value store alone accounts for at least 176.41 GiB in the larger run. Its total excludes the frontier, seen membership, worker arenas and allocator overhead. The 761 checked proof obligations establish the configured invariant independently of this graph size.
